intro.title: Reading: Work and Life
intro.explanation: Read about work situations and daily life using more complex grammar patterns.
intro.cultureNote: Work-life balance (ワークライフバランス) has become an important topic in Japan. Many companies are trying to reduce overtime.

items.passage: 私は去年から東京の会社で働いています。毎日電車で通勤しています。一時間ぐらいかかります。大変ですが、仕事は面白いです。
items.translation: I have been working at a company in Tokyo since last year. I commute by train every day. It takes about one hour. It's tough, but the work is interesting.

questions.question: How does the speaker feel about the job?

items.passage: 先週、会社の人と飲み会がありました。新しい同僚が来たので、歓迎会をしました。日本料理のお店でおいしい物をたくさん食べました。
items.translation: Last week there was a drinking party with people from the company. Because a new colleague came, we had a welcome party. We ate a lot of delicious food at a Japanese restaurant.

items.passage: 最近、残業が多くて疲れています。週末はゆっくり休みたいです。そして、好きな映画を見たいです。
items.translation: Recently, I have a lot of overtime and I'm tired. I want to rest slowly on the weekend. And I want to watch a movie I like.

questions.question: What does the speaker want to do on the weekend?

intro.title: Reading: Culture and Seasons
intro.explanation: Read about Japanese seasonal events and cultural practices.
intro.cultureNote: Japan has a strong tradition of seasonal awareness (季節感). Many activities and foods are associated with specific seasons.

items.passage: 日本の春は桜が有名です。三月の終わりから四月の初めに咲きます。日本人は桜の下でお弁当を食べたり、お酒を飲んだりします。これをお花見と言います。
items.translation: Spring in Japan is famous for cherry blossoms. They bloom from the end of March to the beginning of April. Japanese people eat lunch boxes and drink sake under the cherry blossoms. This is called ohanami.

questions.question: What is ohanami?
options: Viewing cherry blossoms while eating and drinking

items.passage: 日本の夏はとても暑くて湿度が高いです。暑さを避けるために、山や海に行く人が多いです。夏祭りでは花火を見ることができます。
items.translation: Japanese summers are very hot and humid. Many people go to the mountains or sea to escape the heat. At summer festivals you can see fireworks.

questions.question: What can you see at summer festivals?

items.passage: 秋になると、紅葉がきれいです。京都や日光は紅葉の名所として有名です。赤や黄色の葉っぱがとても美しいです。
items.translation: When autumn comes, the fall foliage is beautiful. Kyoto and Nikko are famous as fall foliage spots. The red and yellow leaves are very beautiful.

questions.question: Which places are famous for fall foliage?

items.passage: お正月は日本で一番大切な休日です。家族で集まって、おせち料理を食べます。神社にお参りに行く人も多いです。
items.translation: New Year's is the most important holiday in Japan. Families gather and eat osechi cuisine. Many people also go to visit shrines.

questions.question: What is the most important holiday in Japan?
What do families do during New Year's?

intro.title: Reading: Technology and Communication
intro.explanation: Read about technology in daily life and how people communicate.
intro.cultureNote: Japan is known for advanced technology, but also maintains many traditional communication customs like sending New Year's cards.

items.passage: 最近はスマートフォンで何でもできるようになりました。買い物もできるし、電車の時間も調べられます。便利になりましたが、使い過ぎに注意しなければなりません。
items.translation: Recently, smartphones have made it possible to do anything. You can shop and check train times. It has become convenient, but you must be careful not to use them too much.

questions.question: What can you do with a smartphone according to the passage?
What warning does the passage give?
options: Be careful not to use them too much

items.passage: 日本ではLINEというアプリがとても人気です。友達や家族とメッセージを送ったり、電話をしたりできます。かわいいスタンプも人気の理由の一つです。
items.translation: In Japan, an app called LINE is very popular. You can send messages and make calls with friends and family. Cute stamps are one reason for its popularity.

questions.question: What is one reason LINE is popular?

items.passage: 日本ではまだ年賀状を送る習慣があります。十二月に書いて、一月一日に届くように送ります。最近はメールで送る人も増えています。
items.translation: In Japan, there is still a custom of sending New Year's cards. You write them in December and send them to arrive on January 1st. Recently, more people are sending them by email.

questions.question: When should New Year's cards arrive?
What recent change is mentioned?
options: More people send them by email
